heading.label: Chapter heading · Should you train at all?

blocks.label: Paragraph · Fine-tuning exists for the cases where no published model does…
blocks.md: Fine-tuning exists for the cases where no published model does what you need. Knowing when that is saves weeks.

blocks.label: Label · When it's worth it
Card title · A model misses your material
Paragraph · Some genres break generic separators. Metal is the classic exam…
blocks.md: Some genres break generic separators. Metal is the classic example: so many overlapping sounds that most models smear instruments into each other. Roformers do fairly well, but they come with trade-offs — bleed, dullness, or a target that does not match what you want.

blocks.label: Label · When it isn't
Card title · An existing model is already close
blocks.md: An existing model is already close

blocks.label: Paragraph · If a released checkpoint gets you 90% of the way, an ensemble o…
blocks.md: If a released checkpoint gets you 90% of the way, an ensemble or a different model will usually beat a from-scratch training run that costs GPU rent and weeks of your attention.

blocks.label: Label · The realistic version
Card title · Fine-tune first, pre-train last
Paragraph · Fine-tuning shifts an existing model toward your data and conve…
blocks.md: Fine-tuning shifts an existing model toward your data and converges in days. Training from nothing is dramatically slower and its early metrics look terrible — by design. Start at the shallow end.

blocks.label: Subheading · What you need, in one line
blocks.md: What you need, in one line

blocks.label: Paragraph · A computer with an NVIDIA GPU (required — AMD and Apple GPUs ar…
blocks.md: A computer with an **NVIDIA GPU** (required — AMD and Apple GPUs are not supported by the training stack), at least **8 GB of VRAM** and a reasonably fast card; or a rented GPU from [vast.ai](https://vast.ai), [runpod.io](https://runpod.io) and similar. Plus Python, which you can grab from [python.org](https://www.python.org/downloads/).

blocks.label: Label · Is 8 GB enough?
Paragraph · For pre-training, or for shifting an existing model's target, a…
blocks.md: For *pre-training*, or for shifting an existing model's target, a small card can work — slowly. For real training runs, no: rent cloud compute. A single Roformer at batch size 4 can fill an entire 140 GB H200, so treat small VRAM as a prototyping budget, not a training budget.

blocks.label: Subheading · Can you do this with no prior knowledge?
blocks.md: Can you do this with no prior knowledge?

blocks.label: Paragraph · Yes. That is the entire reason this guide exists. The repositor…
blocks.md: Yes. That is the entire reason this guide exists. The repository's own documentation describes the training scripts accurately but never spells out the actual "how to" — which file goes where, which argument matters, and what the numbers scrolling past your screen mean. That is the gap this guide fills.

blocks.label: Label · Scope
Paragraph · This covers everything learned over months of training, plus th…
blocks.md: This covers everything learned over months of training, plus the fixes contributed by the community. It is not the final word: separation research moves fast, and there is always more to learn. Treat it as a solid starting map, not a contract.
